framework.summary: Prefer uranium exposures that combine resource quality, financing credibility, jurisdictional strength and a plausible path to contracted production. The strongest risk-adjusted exposures remain established producers/fuel-cycle infrastructure, with select development projects promoted only when permitting and financing risk materially improve.

ideas.name: Cameco
ideas.thesis: Cameco remains the highest-quality broad uranium exposure in the stack because it combines operating uranium assets, contracting leverage and Westinghouse participation rather than depending on one future mine start.
ideas.catalysts: Long-term uranium contracting, Western fuel-security demand, reactor restarts/new builds and Westinghouse growth.
ideas.risks: Uranium-price cyclicality, mine execution and premium valuation.
ideas.researchNote: Retains the highest risk-adjusted standing in the uranium sleeve despite stronger development-stage optionality elsewhere.

ideas.name: Centrus Energy
ideas.thesis: Centrus is strategically scarce U.S. enrichment and HALEU infrastructure. It is less about uranium beta and more about rebuilding a domestic nuclear-fuel supply chain.
ideas.catalysts: U.S. enrichment awards, HALEU scale-up and nuclear-fuel reshoring.
ideas.risks: Government-contract dependence, execution and valuation volatility.
ideas.researchNote: Still the cleanest scarcity-infrastructure expression in the fuel cycle.

ideas.name: NexGen Energy
ideas.thesis: NexGen now clears the Power Stack promotion bar because Rook I has final construction approval, site construction has begun, and strategic financing discussions appear to be broadening beyond conventional equity/debt. The Arrow deposit offers unusually large, high-grade uranium optionality in a top-tier jurisdiction, but it remains a project-finance and construction execution story rather than a current producer.
ideas.catalysts: Securing roughly $1bn of project financing, potential strategic investment or offtake support, continued construction progress, uranium contracting and rising nuclear demand tied to energy security and data-centre power growth.
ideas.risks: Large funding requirement, dilution or restrictive financing terms, construction/cost overruns, uranium-price cyclicality, long lead time to production and a valuation that already discounts substantial future success.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Higher upside and higher execution risk than Cameco. Treat NXE as a development-stage satellite position rather than replacing CCJ as the uranium core. Strong recent share-price appreciation raises entry-risk even as strategic validation improves.
ideas.researchNote: Rook I received its final federal licence to prepare site and construct in March 2026. NexGen says the feasibility plan contemplates 239.6M lb of probable reserves and 233.6M lb of recovered yellowcake over an 11-year mine life. Reuters reported on August 17 that construction has begun and NexGen is seeking about $1bn within nine months, including discussions with BHP over a possible equity stake. That materially improves the strategic-validation side of the thesis while leaving financing risk explicit.

sources.label: Reuters — NexGen financing and BHP discussions, Aug. 17, 2026

portfolioRead: CCJ remains the core producer/nuclear-services exposure, LEU remains the strategic enrichment scarcity play, and NXE is now the preferred higher-beta development-stage satellite. Do not treat NXE financing discussions as completed financing until terms are announced.
